reasoning: Both patches address answer-form boundaries, so their nonredundant guidance is consolidated into one replacement of the existing personal-name rule. The replacement balances including identifiers needed for clarity with avoiding unnecessary expansions, and also covers requested aliases and common-noun specificity.

edits.target: Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component.
edits.content: For names and titles, use the established answer form supported by the clue: include surnames, regnal numerals, or other identifying qualifiers when needed, but do not automatically expand to a longer official variant or substitute a familiar nickname for a formal name directly supported by context. If asked for a nickname, epithet, or alias, give that requested label without reattaching a generic type word; supply only a missing name component when asked to complete a supplied name. For common nouns, match the clue's level of generality rather than adding a narrower subtype or descriptive phrase, while retaining qualifiers needed to identify the requested entity.
